question: How much Cartesian Gaussian noise can pointwise intrinsic GAD tolerate while recovering the same LJ7 saddle family?

optimizer.name: pointwise intrinsic smooth-index GAD
optimizer.strict_gate: projected n_neg(lambda < -1e-4) == 1 and Cartesian component fmax < 0.01

reference: LJ7 pentagonal-bipyramid minimum pushed by 0.26 in mass-weighted mode 0, then converged by the tested optimizer

panels.saddle: Gaussian coordinate noise added to the converged reference saddle
panels.pushed: the same paired noise realization added to the targeted mode-pushed minimum

seed_rule: 20260726 + sample_id; identical standard-normal perturbation is scaled across noise levels and paired across panels
primary_outcome: strict TS convergence followed by valid two-branch downhill relaxation to the same unordered endpoint-basin pair as the reference event

downhill_validation.procedure: Displace 0.03 sigma in both signs of the final mass-weighted unstable mode, then minimize physical LJ energy with analytic gradients using L-BFGS-B.
downhill_validation.endpoint_gate: projected n_neg == 0 and Cartesian component fmax < 1e-5
downhill_validation.pair_matching: unordered endpoint energies within 1e-4 and sorted pair-distance fingerprint RMS within 1e-3
downhill_validation.terminology: This is two-branch downhill endpoint validation, not a discretized intrinsic-reaction-coordinate integration.

reference_family_classifier.role: secondary TS-geometry diagnostic; it does not define the primary correct-event outcome

reporting: correct endpoint-event rate with Wilson 95% interval

execution.packing: one exclusive full-node Slurm step containing 192 independently bound one-core shard tasks; no nested Python pool

result.interpretation: Noise primarily increases saddle/event diversity rather than causing local optimizer failure.
result.high_noise_boundary: At 1.5 sigma, near-flat and fragmented fractions rise to 17-22% and barrier q95 exceeds 4 epsilon.
